variants.label: full room-packing pass: herringbone stacking plus I and O pressed flat
variants.architecture: Pure geometry on the packed-storage machine. Blocks 1-4 stacked with zero gap rows using herringbone offsets (each room offset sideways so its wall sits on the row adjacent to its neighbour's, sharing no cell, with the pipe leaving through the resulting overhang into a side wall). O pressed flat against block 4's left wall, reached through the overhang below it. I moved right 2 and up 1 so its right wall abuts block 1, its pipe leaving through the overhang beneath it -- which freed columns 0-1 entirely.
variants.verdict: TEAM BEST for memory: 27.8M -> 23,344,360. Footprint 1,369 -> 1,156 with the machine untouched.

variants.label: packed-storage machine (teammate's; recovered from a paste, was not in the repo)
variants.architecture: Five machine rooms, packed cell storage using 21-bit masks (`2097151`), shifts and `&`/`~` rather than the 100-value FIFO ring of the memory_00..03 line.

source.note: Committed here because it existed only on the contest server and in chat -- no repo copy.

liveSubmission.score: ~27,800,000 (reported by the team; submitted outside this line)

variants.geometryChecked: squeeze (rows/cols/both) and per-room edge trim all return it unchanged -- no empty row, column or room edge exists. fp 1369 is a perfect square; both dimensions bind.

variants.label: top room trimmed, right-edge pipes slid in, bottom room's ports moved to its right wall
variants.architecture: Three steps. (1) The top room's six empty right columns are trimmed; the one read this broke -- row 4 column 24, which preferred the I pipe by a single step -- is fixed by bringing the I pipe in through the BOTTOM wall at column 14 instead of the left wall (solving the room's six reads as distance inequalities gives a feasible window of columns 12-24). (2) The two right-edge pipes, left 6 cells longer by the trim, have their verticals slid into the freed columns: width 46 -> 40 and both pipes end up SHORTER than they began (91->87, 67->63). (3) The bottom room has exactly one incoming and one outgoing pipe, so resolution is trivial and the wall is free to choose: both are re-routed through its RIGHT wall into the freed columns, which deletes rows 43-45 entirely.
variants.verdict: SUPERSEDED by memory_04 (~27.8M). This was the pipeline-ring line; the geometry work on it was correct but applied to a baseline already beaten 3x.

variants.label: mechanical squeeze of empty rows/columns
variants.architecture: Whole-program squeeze via src/littleman/alexey_squeeze.py (rows only -- the column pass breaks it 2/7): every row made only of ' ' and '|', and every column made only of ' ' and '-', is deleted. No room re-laid, no pipe re-routed. Shortens each room interior and each vertical pipe it crosses by one cell; the walk is identical apart from being shorter, which is why ticks fall too.
variants.verdict: SUPERSEDED by memory_04 (~27.8M). This was the pipeline-ring line; the geometry work on it was correct but applied to a baseline already beaten 3x.

variants.label: block1+block2 folded, room4 de-columned, block5 magnetised left
variants.architecture: Three independent geometry moves on memory_06's packed-storage machine, no algorithm change. (1) Block 2 folded width-only 4x29 -> 4x21 by re-dealing its straight-line body across the same rows. (2) Block 1 folded 5x29 -> 5x17 using the perimeter-corridor layout for its single `d` branch (docs/alexey-room-folding.md sec.4). (3) Block 4's three empty interior columns removed and block 5 slid two columns left into the freed space, with both of its pipes re-routed by src/littleman/alexey_piperoute.py at their original lengths (28->29, 19) so no buffer shrank.
variants.verdict: BEST. Width now 32 and height 31 -- height binds, so further width folds (block 3 is 7x26) are banked, not cashed, until a row comes out.

variants.label: block 3 re-laid 26->23 wide; block 5 slid left
variants.architecture: Block 3 (50 instruction cells, one `d`) re-laid with the perimeter-corridor pattern: prologue + d + the short BP==0 arm on the perimeter, the 34-cell BP>0 arm serpentined through the inside, both arms converging on the bottom-right corner. Its two pipes both meet the LEFT wall and it has one pipe each way (port freedom), so the fold needed no pipe work at all. Block 5 then slid one column left and its two pipes were re-routed in separate lanes (cols 28-30 for the inbound, 24-27 for the outbound) at 30 and 21 cells -- both slightly longer than before, never shorter.

localValidation.note: tick counts identical to memory_07 in all seven cases

variants.verdict: BEST. Both dimensions are now 31 and block 4 is what holds them: 15 of the 31 rows and 21 of the 31 columns. Everything else is folded out.

variants.label: block 4: loop units and TAIL pulled in toward the instructions
variants.architecture: Profiling showed block 4 is the bottleneck (100% busy, every other room idle 65-82% of the time waiting on it) and that 55.6% of its ticks are spent walking cells that execute nothing. The loop units themselves are at their geometric floor (8 cells for 4 operations), so the work went into the gaps: loop2 moved from rel cols 14-17 to 11-14, loop3 from 14-17 to 11-14, B4's row pulled in to end at rel 14, and TAIL's two legs pulled from rel 3-18 to rel 6-16. Columns rel 4 and 6 kept clear -- they carry X1's clockwise descent and X2's counter-clockwise halt path. Every r/s zone re-audited cell by cell against memory_08; all fifteen unchanged.

variants.label: block 4 one row shorter; block 5 slid left
variants.architecture: With the interior tightened, block 4's carriage-return row could go: B0's loop unit moved to rel cols 16-18 so d1's straight jump falls down the now-clear rel column 18 to the bottom return row instead of needing a row of its own. Block 4 15 rows -> 14. The O pipe had to move -- its old attachment sat beside the new bottom-left corner -- and went to the TOP of the left wall, which also separates the write zones with more margin. Block 5 then slid one column left and its two pipes were re-routed in disjoint lanes (cols 27-29 inbound, 24-26 outbound).
variants.verdict: BEST. 19,230,331 -> 17,236,875 overall. Both dimensions now 30; block 4 is 14x21 and still holds them.

note: Alexey research line for memory. memory_06 is the current best at 23,344,360 (34x32), reached from memory_04 (37x37, ~27.8M) purely by room packing -- no machine logic touched. Intermediates in submissions/memory/room-packing/.
